newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products--Gulf gasoline diffs extend drop.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products--Gulf gasoline diffs extend drop.

text.p: U.S. Gulf regular gasoline differentials slid lower again Friday, extending the drop that started after the pipeline scheduling deadline Wednesday.
However, New York Harbor and Midcontinent levels were largely unchanged on the day in subdued trading, according to market players.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained 0.32 cent to settle at 57.40 cents a gallon and July heating oil gained 0.02 cent to end at 51.65 cents a gallon.
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline changed hands at 2.85 cents under the July NYMEX, down about 0.50 cent from late Thursday levels.
"There were only a few stragglers around buying today," one Gulf player said, referring to the quiet market conditions following scheduling deadlines on the Colonial Pipeline earlier this week.
"Once (the shorts) covered positions, they didn't want to do anything else," the trader added.
Nearby M1 gasoline differentials have shed nearly 2.00 cents since refiner buying drove them higher Wednesday.
Prompt reformulated A1 gasoline tracked the weakness in the M1, according to market watchers, slipping to about 0.75 cent under the July NYMEX.
Conventional regular M2 gasoline differentials weakened modestly, with prompt barrels trading at 2.60 cents under the July NYMEX, the low end of the range seen late yesterday.
However, market activity remained thin throughout the day, with most market players remaining on the sidelines.
Prompt reformulated A2 barrels were talked slightly weaker, though no deals were reported.
Some strength was seen in the prompt 54-grade jet fuel, which traded at 1.75 cents over the July NYMEX heating oil, though little activity was noted there.

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline markets remained steady at lower numbers on Friday amid quiet activity ahead of the weekend. Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials were a half cent lower for the day, trading between 5.60 to 5.75 cents.
Chicago unleaded was down 0.20 cent at 4.00 to 4.30 cents over July NYMEX.
